newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end down, TEPCO 10-yr bond launch caps upside.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end down, TEPCO 10-yr bond launch caps upside.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly down, but off lows on Tuesday, as the results of a 20-year JGB auction were better than expected, traders said.
"Major foreign and domestic brokerage houses bid aggressively at the auction, and the results look pretty good," said a trader for a foreign brokerage house.

The September was weak, however, as market players were worried that the market may have a difficult time absorbing upcoming issues of corporate straight bonds by companies such as Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc, traders said.
The September ended at 124.71, down from the previous day's close of 124.83. Turnover was 34,434 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.315 percent as of 0648 GMT, up from the previous day's close of 2.285 percent.
Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) launched 100 billion yen worth of 2.625 percent 10-year straight bonds in the afternoon.
Traders said the coupon rate for TEPCO's 10-year issue was too low to attract strong demand from investors.
The coupon rate for TEPCO's 10-year issue was set six basis points above the yield of the 197th JGB, market sources said.
TEPCO and Chugoku Electric Power Co Inc are expected to launch straight bonds on Wednesday, traders said.
TEPCO is expected to launch 20-year bonds, they said.
"The upcoming launches of corporate bonds are capping the upside of JGBs," said a trader for a major brokerage house.

Although some say that the September has already seen its near-term bottom of 124.58 on Tuesday, selling of 10-year JGBs on Tuesday and the increasing supply of bonds may mean a larger fall can be expected, the first trader said.
"Market players are not sure right now of the level at which they should be buying 10-year JGBs," he said.

Selling of 10-year JGBs has made it hard to buy in that zone currently, and this afternoon's TEPCO 10-year bond launch as well as the upcoming launch of 10-year euroyen bonds by Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp are likely to dampen sentiment further, the trader said.
Some investors were detected selling 10-year JGBs for medium-term JGBs, said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
There was talk that an agricultural financial institution had sold long-term JGBs both in the morning and afternoon, the first trader said.
In the morning session, JGB futures fell on hedge selling ahead of the 20-year bond auction.

They received support, however, from comments by Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka saying he supports the view expressed by the BOJ governor that the central bank will maintain its current monetary policy.
MOF's offer of 400 billion yen worth of 3.1 percent 20-year JGBs produced a lowest price of 99.50 and an average price of 99.57.
The Industrial Bank of Japan said it will cut its July long-term prime rate to 2.7 percent from 2.9 percent in June.
